name: Kali Linux
description: Debian-based distribution built for penetration testing, digital forensics and security research.
fullDescription: Kali Linux is a Debian-based distribution maintained by Offensive Security and designed for security professionals, penetration testers and digital forensics. It includes a large collection of security tools.
cons: Not ideal as a first desktop Linux
guide: Use Kali for authorized security testing and learning. For everyday desktop use, choose a general-purpose distribution instead.

name: MX Linux
description: Fast, stable and resource-friendly Debian-based desktop distribution.
fullDescription: MX Linux combines a stable Debian base with practical graphical tools and a lightweight desktop experience. It is a strong choice for older computers and users who want a traditional desktop.
guide: A great choice for an older laptop. Try the Xfce edition first and customize it after installation.

name: Nobara Linux
description: Fedora-based desktop distribution tuned for gaming, streaming and creative workloads.
fullDescription: Nobara Linux is a Fedora-based project focused on making gaming, streaming and creative workflows easier by providing practical patches and preconfigured components.
guide: If your main goal is gaming on Linux, Nobara is worth testing in a virtual machine or spare drive before committing to it.

name: Bazzite
description: Gaming-focused immutable Linux image designed for desktops and handheld gaming PCs.
fullDescription: Bazzite is an image-based Fedora Atomic desktop focused on gaming. It provides a SteamOS-like experience while supporting desktop PCs, handhelds and a wide range of gaming hardware.
guide: Choose the image matching your hardware, especially for handhelds. Keep the system updated and use the built-in gaming tools.

name: Garuda Linux
description: Arch-based distribution with a flashy desktop, gaming tools and performance-oriented defaults.
fullDescription: Garuda Linux is an Arch-based distribution offering several desktop editions and a strong focus on performance, visual customization and gaming.
guide: Pick the KDE Dr460nized edition for the signature look, or choose a lighter edition for older hardware.

name: NixOS
description: Declarative Linux distribution with reproducible system configuration and a unique package manager.
fullDescription: NixOS uses the Nix package manager and declarative configuration to make system setups reproducible, rollback-friendly and easy to version control.
guide: Start in a VM and learn the Nix language and configuration model before installing it as your main OS.

name: Alpine Linux
description: Tiny, security-oriented Linux distribution popular for containers, servers and embedded systems.
fullDescription: Alpine Linux is a lightweight distribution designed with security and simplicity in mind. Its small footprint makes it especially popular for containers and minimal servers.
guide: Excellent for containers and minimal servers. Learn Alpine's busybox and apk workflow before using it for production systems.

name: Rocky Linux
description: Enterprise Linux distribution compatible with Red Hat Enterprise Linux workflows.
fullDescription: Rocky Linux is an open-source enterprise operating system designed to be compatible with Red Hat Enterprise Linux. It is suitable for servers, infrastructure and organizations that value long support cycles.
guide: Use Rocky when you need a stable enterprise-style environment and long maintenance windows.

name: AlmaLinux
description: Community-driven enterprise Linux focused on long-term stability and RHEL compatibility.
fullDescription: AlmaLinux is an open-source enterprise Linux distribution intended to provide a stable, production-ready platform compatible with RHEL application ecosystems.
guide: A strong choice for server labs, homelabs and enterprise-style development environments.

name: Void Linux
description: Independent rolling-release Linux distribution known for simplicity and the runit init system.
fullDescription: Void Linux is an independently developed rolling-release distribution. It uses the XBPS package system and runit service supervision, making it attractive to users who want a different approach to Linux administration.
guide: Try Void in a VM first. Its service management and package tools differ from Debian and Arch.

name: EndeavourOS
description: Lightweight Arch-based distribution that stays close to upstream Arch while simplifying installation.
fullDescription: EndeavourOS provides a convenient installer and a light layer of customization while keeping users close to the Arch ecosystem and ArchWiki.
guide: Great next step after Linux Mint or Ubuntu if you want to learn Arch without starting from a manual install.

name: Puppy Linux
description: Extremely lightweight Linux family designed to run well on older hardware and from removable media.
fullDescription: Puppy Linux is a family of small Linux distributions designed for low-resource computers. It can run from USB or RAM and is useful for rescue, testing and older PCs.
cons: Not ideal for every modern workload
guide: Perfect for reviving an old laptop. Boot from USB first and test hardware compatibility before installing.

name: Tails
description: Portable Debian-based live system designed to preserve privacy and anonymity.
fullDescription: Tails is a live operating system designed to help users preserve privacy and anonymity. It routes applications through Tor and is intended to leave as little trace as practical on the computer it runs from.
guide: Read the official documentation carefully and verify the download before creating your USB.

name: Qubes OS
description: Security-focused operating system that isolates tasks into separate virtual machines.
fullDescription: Qubes OS uses virtualization to compartmentalize applications and workflows into isolated qubes. It is designed for users who prioritize security boundaries over simplicity.
guide: Use compatible hardware and follow the official installation guide. Qubes works best with ample RAM and virtualization support.

name: Ubuntu Studio
description: Ubuntu flavor tailored for audio, video, graphics and content creation.
fullDescription: Ubuntu Studio is an official Ubuntu flavor designed for creative professionals and hobbyists. It includes software and configuration aimed at audio production, graphics, photography and video work.
guide: Ideal if you want a ready-made Linux creative workstation. Install your preferred creative applications and configure storage for projects.

name: Kubuntu
description: Ubuntu flavor featuring the powerful and highly customizable KDE Plasma desktop.
fullDescription: Kubuntu combines Ubuntu's package ecosystem with KDE Plasma. It offers a polished desktop, deep customization and a familiar workflow for many Windows users.
cons: KDE uses more resources than lightweight desktops
guide: Choose Kubuntu if you want Ubuntu compatibility with a desktop you can customize heavily.

name: Lubuntu
description: Lightweight Ubuntu flavor designed for speed and lower-resource computers.
fullDescription: Lubuntu combines Ubuntu's ecosystem with the lightweight LXQt desktop. It is useful for older laptops and users who prefer a fast, simple interface.
cons: Less visual polish than heavier desktops
guide: A good first choice for an older PC. Test the live environment before installation.

name: Raspberry Pi OS
description: Official Debian-based operating system optimized for Raspberry Pi computers.
fullDescription: Raspberry Pi OS is the official operating system for Raspberry Pi computers. It provides a lightweight desktop and extensive hardware-specific documentation and tools.
cons: Some desktop software differs from x86
guide: Use Raspberry Pi Imager to install the correct image for your board and start with the recommended desktop edition.
